items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, List of Answers on Topics 54:1
items.html: The coarseness of phase one of direct light is called “reception by way of Keter.” The coarseness of phase two is called distancing. The coarseness of phase three is called a window and a narrow hole. The coarseness of phase four is called a window and a narrow hole together with distancing. (Chapter 1, Item 4)
